main_text.p: nuntiarunt, dicuntur seruasse illos, adeoq; Seruatores illorum; Paulus enim Rom. 11. v. 14. scribit: Si quo modo ad aemulandum provocem carnem meam, & seruem aliquot ex illis. 1. Corinth. 9. v. 22. Omnibus factus sum omnia, ut omnino aliquos seruem. 1. Tim. 4. Attende tibi ipsi & doctrinae; perfiste in his. Hoc enim faciens, & te ipsum seruabis, & eos qui te audiunt. Jacobus in fine Epistolae suae sic ait: Qui converti fecerit peccatorem ab errore viae suae, seruabit animam a morte: Multo igitur magis unigenitus Dei Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, & ab initio ad hoc docendi munus obeundum a Patre (qui etiam per eum loquutus est) delectus, viam salutis annuntiavit, atq; in cuius nomine Apostoli ab ipso missi Evangelium praedicarunt, Seruator noster dicitur.

Insufficientem autē dico hunc Seruandi modum; si seorsim accipiatur, ut qui Mediatoris, Conciliatoris & Seruatoris (qui partes scilicet diffidentes reconciliat seipsum interponendo Medium, satisfaciendo pro offensa, pròq; ea deprecando) Naturam & officium ἀλλ constituat neutiquam. Soli quippe fi-bi hoc sicut.At insufficient, si sola accipitur, at ab adversarium non sola, sed cum Exemplo, obsignatione & communicatione sumitur. Necdum tamen est suf-ficiens.

page.notes: The page is a scan of a 17th-century Latin theological text with the running head "CAP. III. SECT. I." and page number 244 at top right. Several words in the right-margin note are blurred and uncertain; the note text is transcribed with [?] where doubtful. The Greek word in the body (ἀλλ...) is partially cut off by the scan and is uncertain. The main text's final lines and the margin note at lower right are partly illegible due to damage and show-through, and the transcription of those lines is approximate. The catchword "bi hoc" and the signature "D 2" appear at the foot.
